lesson.name: Learn The Indian Defenses And The Black Knights' Tango
lesson.description: Learn the ideas behind the Indian Defenses and take and find out how to play both sides of the Black Knights' Tango.

{Black has captured a poisoned pawn. How can White win material?} 5. Qd4 {
[%wrong There's a better move to win material. Try again and look for a
winning fork.] [%hint Attack both knights with your queen.]} (5. Qe2 $5 {
This is a good choice, but it's even stronger to fork the black knights. How
should you do it?}) 5... d6 {Good idea! What's next?} 6. Qxe4 {[%wrong There's
a better option. Try again and look for a strong capture.] [%hint Capture an
undefended piece.] Well played! White wins a knight and should win the game.} *

{How did GM Benjamin take advantage of White's slow development?} 7... Bb4+ {
[%wrong There's a better option. Try again and look for a strong check.] 
[%hint Develop a bishop with a check.]} (7... exd5 $5 8. cxd5 {This is
playable, but there's a check that's stronger. Try to find it.}) (7... Qh4+ $2
8. g3 {Black won't be able to save the knight and queen. Try again and look
for a stronger check.}) (7... f5 $5 {This is playable, but there's a check
that's stronger. Try to find it.}) 8. Kd1 {White had no good way to keep the
right to castle. How should Black save the e4-knight?} f5 {[%wrong There's a
better option. Try again and look for a way to defend your knight on e4.] 
[%hint Defend your knight with a pawn.] Good work! Black's knight is strong in
the center and White's exposed king eventually decided the game in Potter -
Benjamin, 2003.} (8... exd5 $2 9. cxd5 {White's big center may become an issue.
Try again and look for a better way to defend your knight.}) (8... Nc5 $2 9. a3
{At least one black piece will soon be trapped on the queenside. Try again and
look for a way to protect your knight.}) *

{How did Karpov save his h-pawn?} 18. h5 {[%wrong Black wins material. Try
again and look for a way to save your h-pawn.] [%hint Attack the g6-knight.]}
Nf8 {Nearly every black piece is stuck on the back rank. How did Karpov make
another strong threat?} 19. Rg1 {[%wrong There's a stronger move. Try again
and look for a precise threat.] [%hint Attack a pawn on the half-open g-file.]
Well done! Black is horribly passive and White went on to win in Karpov -
Chevallier, 1993.} (19. Qe3 $5 {This is reasonable, but it's stronger to
attack the g7-pawn. How should you do it?}) *

{How should Black win material?} 8... Bxf2+ {[%wrong There's a better option.
Try again and look for a way to win material.] [%hint Sacrifice a bishop to
decoy White's king into a fork.]} (8... Ng4 $5 {This is good choice, but let's
start the combination with a capture. How should you do it?}) 9. Kxf2 {White
would have been better off leaving the bishop on f2, but Black is doing well
anyway. After Kxf2 Black wins more material. How should you do it?} Ng4+ {
[%wrong There's a better option. Try again and look for a winning fork.] 
[%hint Fork White's king and queen.]} 10. Ke1 {Great move! What's next?} Nxe5 {
[%wrong There's a better option. Try again and look for a strong capture.] 
[%hint Capture the queen.] Good work! Black soon wins with the extra queen.} *

{What strong pawn sacrifice did GM Ivanchuk find to open the position and
start an attack?} 16. c5 {[%wrong There's a better move. Try again and look
for strong pawn sacrifice.] [%hint Sacrifice a pawn to distract a defender of
the e5-pawn.] Good choice! After dxc4, Ivanchuk's Nc4 kept a strong initiative,
although Bc2 would be even more effective. White won a long game in Ivanchuk -
Bauer, 2012.} (16. dxc6 $2 bxc6 {White has only a small advantage. Try again
and look for Ivanchuk's powerful pawn sacrifice.}) (16. g3 $2 Ng6 {White has
only a small advantage. Try again and look for Ivanchuk's more powerful pawn
sacrifice.}) *

{White has moved too many pawns and Black can win material. How should you do
it?} 11... Bd4 {[%wrong There's a better move. Try again and look for a way to
pin a white piece.] [%hint Pin the c3-knight on the long diagonal.]} 12. Bb2 {
Good start! How can you win material?} Bxc3 {[%wrong There's a better option.
Try again and look for a strong capture.] [%hint Remove the defender of
White's e4-pawn.]} (12... Nxe4 $2 13. Nxe4 {The b2-bishop is defended and
White wins material. Try again and look for a stronger capture.}) (12... b5 $5
{Black is doing well, but there's an immediate capture to win material. Try to
find it.}) (12... Bd7 $5 {Black is doing well, but there's an immediate
capture to win material. Try to find it.}) 13. Bxc3 {Well played! What's next?}
Nxe4 {[%wrong There's a better move. Try again and look for a strong capture.]
[%hint Capture an undefended pawn.] Good work! Black wins material with a
great position. We will revisit the game Benitah - Fioramonti, 2016 in the
next challenge.} *

{How should Black continue the attack?} 24... Ngxf3 {[%wrong There's a better
option. Try again and look for a precise capture.] [%hint Sacrifice a knight
to win a pawn and open the g-file for your queen.]} (24... Bxd3 $5 {Black is
doing well, but there's another capture that's stronger. Try to find it.}) (
24... a5 $5 {This is OK, but there's a capture that's stronger. Try to find it.
}) (24... Nxg2 $2 25. Bxf5 {White retains chances to defend. Try again and
look for a stronger knight sacrifice.}) (24... Nhxf3 $2 25. Bxf5 {There's a
much stronger knight sacrifice. Try to find it.}) 25. gxf3 {In the actual game,
White tried Ne4, but couldn't defend down two pawns. How would Black win after
gxf3?} Qg2# {[%wrong There's a way to checkmate, but that's not it. Look at
your checks and try again.] [%hint Look at your checks. Which one is mate?]
Well done!} *

{The knight on c6 is in danger. Where should it go?} 10... Nd4 {[%wrong White
wins material. Try again and look for a strong knight move.] [%hint Centralize
the c6-knight.]} (10... Ne7 $2 {White has the much more active position. Try
again and look for a stronger knight move.}) (10... Na5 $2 11. b4 {The knight
is trapped. Try to find a better square for it.}) (10... Nb8 $2 11. b4 {
White has the much more active position. Try again and look for a stronger
knight move.}) 11. Nxd4 {White wins material, but not for long. What should
Black play?} exd4 {[%wrong There's a better move. Try again and look for a
strong capture.] [%hint Recapture the knight.]} 12. Bxd4 {How should you win
back the lost pawn?} Nxe4 {[%wrong There's a better option. Try again and look
for a precise capture.] [%hint Capture the e4-pawn.]} 13. Bxg7 {Well played!
What should you capture next?} Kxg7 {[%wrong There's a stronger move. Try to
find a precise capture.] [%hint Recapture the bishop.]} (13... Nxc3 $2 14. Bxc3
{White wins material. Try again and look for a stronger capture.}) 14. Nxe4 {
Good move. Keep it up.} Rxe4 {[%wrong There's a better move. Try to find a
good capture.] [%hint Recapture the piece.] Well done! Black has a comfortable
game and went on to win in Popov - Bologan, 2001.} *
